Tennis.title: Alcaraz delivers statement win to reach last eight
Tennis.summary: Carlos Alcaraz continues his return from long-term injury with a hugely impressive fourth-round win against Tommy Paul at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz continued his return from long-term injury with a hugely impressive fourth-round win against Tommy Paul at the US Open. Playing just his fourth competitive singles match after an absence of more than four months, the 23-year-old Spaniard produced a masterful performance to beat American 20th seed Paul 6-4 6-3 6-4.

He has dropped only one set on his way to the last eight in New York and will face American eighth seed Ben Shelton in the quarter-finals. A wrist injury caused Alcaraz to miss both the French Open and Wimbledon earlier this summer.

Tennis.title: Sabalenka overcomes tricky Townsend test at US Open
Tennis.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulates Serena Williams by overcoming Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final.
Tennis.body:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulated Serena Williams as she eventually overpowered American Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final. A topsy-turvy contest featured 10 breaks of serve, but Sabalenka recovered from 3-1 down in the second serve to seal a 6-4 6-3 victory with a fifth consecutive game.

It was the Belarusian's 18th consecutive win at the tournament, extending her three-year unbeaten streak following back-to-back triumphs in 2024 and 2025. Sabalenka, 28, is the first woman to reach six consecutive singles quarter-finals at Flushing Meadows since American great Williams in 2016.

Tennis.body:
Coco Gauff marched into the fourth round of the US Open but compatriots Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys exited on a mixed day for home hopes in New York. Gauff, the most recent American champion in New York in 2023, did not have things all her own way but maintained her bid for a second triumph by overcoming Spain's Cristina Bucsa 6-3 6-4.

However, Keys said she felt "scared" as she slumped to defeat despite leading her third set against China's Zheng Qinwen 5-0, while last year's runner-up Anisimova lost in straight sets.

Tennis.summary: Alex Eala expected to earn ‘crazy’ money in 2027 with her growth even bigger than Emma Raducanu’s Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Few would deny that Alexandra Eala is now one of the biggest stars in tennis, made even more impressive given her relative inexperience on the professional tour. Her fame and notoriety do not align with her time spent near the top of the game, but she still feels deserving of this unrivalled support, wherever she plays.

And, after a relatively promising but inconsistent start to her career, it already feels like she is putting together the results to justify such acclaim. That is why pundits are now predicting Eala to soon be one of the highest-paid female athletes in the world, with Jim Courier and Lindsay Davenport the latest to discuss this phenomenon.

Tennis.title: 'Finally luck is on my side'
Tennis.summary: Zheng Qinwen fights back from 5-0 down in the deciding set and stares down match point to stun American 22nd seed Madison Keys.
Tennis.body:
Zheng Qinwen described her US Open third-round comeback win over Madison Keys as a "very dramatic match" - but that is somewhat of an understatement. The Olympic champion, who had to come through qualifying to reach the main draw, found herself 5-0 and match point down in the third set against Keys.

But Zheng held firm and reeled off seven games in a row to secure a remarkable 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 victory over the 22nd seed and crowd favourite. Keys, who won the 2025 Australian Open, appeared to be cruising towards a commanding victory after wrapping up the opening set in just 23 minutes.

I always think there's things that British tennis could do better. So yes, definitely," said British women's number three Francesca Jones.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu’s US Open triumph five years on, told by her opponents
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu’s US Open triumph five years on, told by her opponents The i Paper
Tennis.body:
FLUSHING MEADOWS — “Is it really five years?” says one player incredulously when I ask them what they were doing the night Emma Raducanu won the US Open. For many of us, it feels like yesterday. Raducanu’s run from qualifying to the title, never achieved at a grand slam before or since, has shaped the last five years in British tennis like few three-week periods ever have. She became and remains this country’s biggest star in women’s tennis, her every match, interview, coaching change and practice session closely followed and scrutinised.

It is typical of the rocky road Raducanu, now 23, has ridden since becoming US Open champion that she is not even here in New York to look back at the half-decade that has passed. The Big Apple has not been a happy hunting ground in that time either: she has won just two matches at this tournament since she won it.

Tennis.title: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka complains of cannabis smell during win over Kamilla Rakhimova to reach fourth round
Tennis.summary: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka complains of cannabis smell during win over Kamilla Rakhimova to reach fourth round Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka complained to the umpire about a strong smell of cannabis that was present duing her third-round win over Kamilla Rakhimova at the US Open. The world No 1 came through in straight sets, beating her unseeded opponent 6-3 6-4 on Louis Armstrong Stadium, but after racing into a 3-0 lead in the opening set, Sabalenka complained to umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore at the first changeover.

"I was like, 'Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around the tennis courts'," Sabalenka told reporters afterwards. "It's a bit tricky to handle that smell while you're trying to compete at your best."

Aryna Sabalenka briefly halted her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova because of a strong smell of cannabis before cruising into the fourth round in New York. Top seed Sabalenka raised the issue after going 3-0 up in the first set against Uzbekistan's Rakhimova, telling umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore that "someone is smoking weed".

The Belarusian asked the umpire to intervene "because it's so strong". Asderaki-Moore spoke to an official on her radio and made a smoking gesture to someone behind her, before play continued.

Tennis.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev endures another gruelling five-set US Open match as he overcomes Quentin Halys at 02:15 local time to reach the third round.

Top seed Alexander Zverev endured another gruelling five-set US Open match as he overcame Quentin Halys at 02:15 local time to reach the third round. French Open champion Zverev is one of the favourites for the title, with world number one Jannik Sinner missing with injury and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz working his way back to fitness.

Tennis.summary: A "battle-tested" Coco Gauff shows grit to keep her bid for a second US Open title alive with victory over Paula Badosa in the second round.
Tennis.body:
A "battle-tested" Coco Gauff showed grit to keep her bid for a second US Open title alive with victory over Paula Badosa in the second round. Fourth seed Gauff had lost her past two matches against Spanish former world number two Badosa, but showed impressive composure in a tough encounter at Flushing Meadows in New York.

American Gauff was twice a break up in the second set and served for the match at 6-5, only to put a volley into the net to send it to a tie-break. After a quick yell of "why?" towards her team, Gauff reset and was solid to close out victory on a second match point.

Tennis.title: Kyrgios given one-month ban for positive cocaine test
Tennis.summary: Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine.
Tennis.body:
Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine. The Australian, 31, was provisionally suspended on 4 August after a sample he submitted during the Mallorca Open in June was found to contain benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Kyrgios told investigators from the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) that he used cocaine at a nightclub in Magaluf in the early hours of 20 June. He played his first-round match at the Mallorca tournament two days later, losing in straight sets to compatriot Adam Walton.

Tennis.title: What is the US Open prize money per round?
Tennis.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team look at the breakdown of a record-breaking prize fund at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
It's a record-breaking year for prize money at the US Open. The total prize money available to players is $108m (£80m), which is 20% more than the 2025 tournament - making it not just the largest-ever US Open prize pot, but the largest in Grand Slam history.

For comparison, the prize fund for Wimbledon this year was £64.2m. Of the US Open prize fund, $2m (£1.47m) goes towards a 'player support programme' after calls from players for athlete welfare across the Grand Slams, which the US Open says is "designed to complement existing end-of-career pension funds" and "will bring a range of benefits for mid-career life events and retirement transitions".

Tennis.title: Monfils wins on 40th birthday as Zverev celebrates at 2am
Tennis.summary: French veteran Gael Monfils is treated to a rendition of Happy Birthday by the US Open crowd as he becomes the oldest man to win a match there since 1992.
Tennis.body:
Most people celebrate their 40th birthday with a slap-up meal or a surprise party. Gael Monfils, the maverick Frenchman who always knows how to have fun on the court, marked his milestone by winning a Grand Slam match at the US Open.

Playing in the final major of his career, Monfils ensured he had a unforgettable night with a 2-6 6-1 6-2 6-0 victory over Paraguayan opponent Adolfo Daniel Vallejo. The former world number six is the oldest man to win a US Open main-draw match since Jimmy Connors - who also won on his 40th birthday in 1992.

Tennis.title: Gauff's flaw forgotten on winning US Open return
Tennis.summary: At last year's US Open, Coco Gauff's serve left her practising in the rain and crying on court - now it is a potent weapon.
Tennis.body:
The sight of a forlorn Coco Gauff hitting serves in the rain on the US Open practice courts became the defining image of her struggles last year. The serving yips were undermining the two-time major champion's talent. Staying out in the persistent drizzle was a sign of how desperate she had become to iron out the major flaw in her game.

Twelve months on, the 22-year-old American has returned to the US Open with a rejuvenated service game - and it was the bedrock of her 6-3 6-4 win over Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez in the New York first round on Tuesday.

Tennis.body:
Be warned: Novak Djokovic has made a fool of those who have doubted him before. Some questioned if the Serb would challenge for the sport's top honours again after he dropped out of the world's top 20 amid a two-year major title drought in 2018.

The 41-year-old Swiss is retiring at the end of the season and looked close to tears as he received a rapturous reception after a straight-set defeat by Italy's Matteo Berrettini.

Wawrinka, who won the US Open in 2016, was initially overlooked by tournament organisers for a wildcard, but was given a last-minute reprieve following American recipient Patrick Kypson's withdrawal.

Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open. Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

Golf.body:
When GOLF’s own Top 100 Teacher Martin Chuck created the Smart Ball, his goal was simple: Make a no-fuss training aid that actually solves a common swing issue. Just put the lanyard around your neck and the Smart Ball helps you keep your arms connected and your body rotating properly.

Since its inception in 2014, the Smart Ball remains wildly popular, and you’re still likely to find it in use on the practice tee at nearly every PGA Tour stop. Chuck has stepped things up with the Smart Ball Sleeve ($57 with a Smart Ball; tourstriker.com) — a clever, wearable accessory that lets you attach the Smart Ball almost anywhere: arms, legs, hips, you name it. And, of course, Chuck’s got video drills to go with it, educating you on exactly how this versatile tool can help you dial in your swing.

Golf.title: Flair, grip and durability? Why Asher checks those boxes
Golf.summary: In 2009, Asher set out to turn golf gloves into a fashion piece, and today the brand offers some of the most stylish gloves on the market. The post Flair, grip and durability? Why Asher checks those boxes appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Too often, we overlook or undervalue just how important our golf glove really is, only to realize how dreadful things can get when it goes bad. For many, a fine Cabretta leather glove — slightly thinner and more moisture-resistant than cowhide — is an essential component not only to playing well and maintaining your hold on the club but also to protecting your hand from calluses and blisters.

In 2009, Asher set out to turn this largely utilitarian accessory into a fashion piece, and today the brand offers some of the most stylish gloves on the market. They’re available in a wide range of colors and sizes for men and women to punch up any on-course outfit. Asher helps you add a little flair to your look while still providing the grip and durability you need.

Golf.title: Can Cleveland's new RTZ2 wedges handle real-world turf? We put them to the test
Golf.summary: Johnny Wunder and Jake Morrow traveled to Pinehurst to put the Cleveland RTZ2 wedges to the "game-time" test. Here are the results. The post Can Cleveland’s new RTZ2 wedges handle real-world turf? We put them to the test appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Wedge testing is a finicky thing. A lot of great work can be done in a fitting bay, without question. But you can’t put a metric for how important getting a bunch of wedges out on a course to just mess around is. You’ve seen us test a bunch of clubs in the technical way, but what about the “feel” way?

Well… Jake and I grabbed an armful of the new Cleveland RTZ2 wedges, kicked off our shoes and walked nine holes at The Cradle at Pinehurst. Sand-dusted turf, short targets, Sunday bags — an honest place to see what a leading edge actually does under pressure. Here’s what we learned.

Golf.body:
Before the Europeans made their historic comeback at the 2012 Ryder Cup at Medinah, fiery Englishman Ian Poulter had to make five consecutie birdies to help him and Rory McIlroy win their Saturday match and trim Team USA’s lead to 10-6 heading into Sunday.

“This has given us a heartbeat,” Poulter said that Saturday night. One day later, the Europeans had stormed back to snatch the Ryder Cup away from the Americans in historic fashion. But the comeback all started with Poulter creating momentum out of thin air for his team to feed off — creating belief.

Golf.title: GB&I make history with first Walker Cup since 2015
Golf.summary: Great Britain and Ireland produce the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States and lift the trophy for the first time since 2015.
Golf.body:
Great Britain and Ireland produced the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States and lift the trophy for the first time since 2015. At Lahinch in Ireland, the USA looked to be on the brink when they swept the morning foursomes to move just three-and-a-half points away from a sixth consecutive victory.

But GB&I picked up seven of the 10 points in the singles to clinch victory by 13-and-a-half points to 12-and-a-half and win for the first time in 11 years. Josh Hill had the winning moment as he defeated world number two Tyler Watts on the final hole of the last match on the course, and that sparked wild celebrations to mark a victory that seemed so unlikely after Sunday morning.

Golf.title: Is the Walker Cup golf's greatest team event? It's been making the case
Golf.summary: The Walker Cup is in a great spot to become golf's greatest team event, because it’s all about the golfers, the golf and the host courses. The post Is the Walker Cup golf’s greatest team event? It’s been making the case appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Did you watch this Walker Cup at Lahinch, in Ireland? Maybe you were one of the 8,000 or so people on hand, watching up close. (Single-day tickets were about $50; kids were free.) Maybe you were watching on Golf Channel, with the American Curtis Cup star Emilia Migliaccio Doran and the former GB&I Walker Cup player Paul McGinley presiding. Poor McGinley, about the most refreshing voice in golf broadcasting today and an Irishman’s Irishman. He must be worn out. He was wearing his big heart on his green sleeve as he practically begged the home 10 to scratch out this half-point or that one.

In the end, his prayers were answered. In this 51st edition of the Walker Cup, the two-day event that unfolds with stunning speed, Great Britain and Ireland defeated a stacked American team, 13.5 to 12.5. Sunday afternoon, in the decisive singles play, GB&I won seven matches, halved two and lost one. GB&I won the event for the first time since 2015. It was amazing.

Golf.title: Team GB&I storms back to shock the U.S. and win the Walker Cup
Golf.summary: Team Great Britain & Ireland won seven of 10 points during Sunday Singles to complete an improbable Walker Cup comeback. The post Team GB&I storms back to shock the U.S. and win the Walker Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Team Great Britain and Ireland are Walker Cup champions once again — and they did so in improbable fashion. Entering the final singles session on Sunday afternoon at Lahinch Golf Club, Team USA looked to be on their way to a sixth consecutive victory in the biennial team competition as they held a 9.5 to 6.5 advantage. However, thanks to a historic final session that saw GB&I win seven of the available 10 points, the team from across the pond completed the comeback for a 13.5 to 12.5 victory.

“I believed in the team the whole time,” said GB&I captain Dean Robertson. “I’m so proud of them. Just so special.” After Team USA swept the morning foursomes session, the three-point lead entering the final session looked all but insurmountable. Needing seven points in the final singles session, GB&I’s margin for error was razor thin. Luckily, many of them saved their best golf for last.

Golf.body:

Golf.title: 5 keys for fixing the 'chicken wing' in your golf swing
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel explains five keys for fixing the dreaded "chicken wing" in your golf swing. The post 5 keys for fixing the ‘chicken wing’ in your golf swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you struggle with a “chicken wing” in your golf swing, I’ve got good news: it can be fixed. Part of the reason it is so important to take lessons from a great instructor is that the chicken wing is often a necessary compensation for an earlier issue in the swing. In other words, simply trying to eliminate the chicken wing may not fix the problem. You first need to understand why it is happening.

Here are five things you can do to fix your chicken-wing swing. If you are looking for a quick fix, a split-hand drill can certainly help with the chicken wing. Because the hands are separated on the grip, the lead elbow will almost automatically fold and point down. This is the opposite of a chicken wing, where the elbows tend to separate as the club is pulled away from the ground. It’s a great drill to help you feel what the lead arm and elbow should be doing through impact and into the release.

Golf.body:

LIV in July filed a notice under the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act that indicated layoffs were likely.

It has been a while since Paul Casey was in this spot, holding a 54-hole lead with a chance to add to his trophy case. But after firing a 7-under 63 on Saturday at Crans-Sur-Sierre Golf Club, Casey will enter Sunday at the Omega European Masters with a three-shot lead.

The last time Casey won a tournament of any sort was the 2021 Dubai Desert Classic. A lot has changed in pro golf since the last time Casey hoisted a trophy. The former World No. 3 left for LIV Golf in 2022. As a member of the Bryson DeChambeau-fronted Crushers, Casey won $31.8 million but never won a solo title, losing twice in a playoff. His last major championship appearance came at the 2022 Open Championship, and his last DP World Tour top 10 was at the Porsche Singapore Classic in 2024.

Golf.title: Add spin to your greenside chip shots with this simple technique
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Jeff Smith explains the simple technique you can use to add spin to your greenside chip shots. The post Add spin to your greenside chip shots with this simple technique appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Every rec player wants to hit chip shots that take one hop and stop on a dime. Good news: It’s easier than it looks. The key is combining an open clubface with a downward angle of attack, and both are achievable with a few simple setup adjustments.

Start by grabbing your highest-lofted wedge and positioning the ball slightly forward in your stance, just below your lead eye. To promote a steeper attack angle, use a modified grip: place all five fingers of your trail hand on the club, then set the index finger of your lead hand over the pinkie of your trail hand to create a reverse overlap. Finally, rotate your trail hand slightly on top of the grip to encourage a more descending angle of attack.

Golf.title: 'Brainless of me': Early scooped putt leads to Walker Cup rules drama
Golf.summary: The 51st Walker Cup started with a meaningful short miss by the World No. 1 and some rules drama after an early scooped putt. The post ‘Brainless of me’: Early scooped putt leads to Walker Cup rules drama appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The first session of the 51st Walker Cup at Lahinch Golf Club wasn’t short on drama. While the Americans are the clear favorites on paper, they face their stiffest test in some time against a Great Britain and Ireland team that is hungry to end Team USA’s five-tournament winning streak. Saturday morning’s foursomes session opened with World No. 1 amateur Preston Stout and Ethan Fang facing Stuart Grehan and Eliot Baker. The two teams traded blows for 15 holes, with Grehan and Baker taking a 1-up lead with three holes to play. But the Americans won 16 and 17 to reach the final hole in position to put an early point on the board.

After GB&I got in with a birdie four on the par-5 18th, Stout had a short birdie putt to tie the hole and win the match for the Americans. But his attempt slid past the hole, and GB&I salvaged a big half-point to open the competition.

Golf.title: New Zealand has become the ultimate golf dream trip. Here's why
Golf.summary: New Zealand has more golf courses per capita than any country other than Scotland, in a setting of unrivaled serenity and beauty. The post New Zealand has become the ultimate golf dream trip. Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
On the world clock, New Zealand is well ahead of the United States. But North American golfers have been catching up. They’ve come to recognize the country as a must-visit, magnetic for the quality and diversity of its courses, the beauty of its landscapes and the welcoming spirit of its people.

That awareness wasn’t born overnight. It began stirring decades ago with the opening of Kauri Cliffs and Cape Kidnappers, luxurious resorts whose seaside layouts, stunning scenery and A-list accommodations remain emblems of New Zealand’s coastal splendor. The more recent arrival of marquee properties like Tara Iti and Te Arai — which combined to deliver three new courses to GOLF’s World Top 100 list — attracted next-level attention that was further magnified by the Covid golf boom. As the spotlight brightened on the North Island, it radiated outward, illuminating a golf scene of remarkable depth and range.

Golf.title: Testing the YouTube famous Takomo Irons. (Hint: They're impressive)
Golf.summary: The curiosity around Takomo irons has been loud. We wanted to find out why — and the results were very impressive The post Testing the YouTube famous Takomo Irons. (Hint: They’re impressive) appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ll just start here: I was late to the Takomo party. I knew the name. I’d seen the irons. I’d seen them all over YouTube and Instagram. I knew Takomo was one of those direct-to-consumer brands that had managed to build a pretty serious following without playing by the traditional golf-equipment rulebook. But knowing about something and actually hitting it are two very different things. There are plenty of golf clubs I’ve looked at, read about and formed an opinion on before ever putting one behind a ball. Then you actually hit them and realize the opinion you had was based on absolutely nothing. Which, to be fair, is kind of how the internet works.

So when I finally got some time with the Takomo irons, I went into it with one question: What’s the catch? Because golf equipment has conditioned us to think that way. If an iron looks premium, feels premium and performs like the stuff hanging on the wall at your local golf shop, we generally expect the price tag to reflect it. That’s just how this has worked for a long time. Good golf equipment costs good golf-equipment money.

Golf.title: Stomach issues again hit Walker Cup. And alternate is on ‘standby’
Golf.summary: Stomach issues again hit the Walker Cup, an amateur event played this year at Lahinch Golf Club in Ireland. And an alternate is on “standby.” The post Stomach issues again hit Walker Cup. And alternate is on ‘standby’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The U.S. Walker Cup team is now “bouncing around,” its captain, Nathan Smith, says. And his players’ stomachs, it appears, have mostly stopped rumbling. On Thursday, two days before this weekend’s amateur event, that features a 10-man American team meeting a 10-man Great Britain and Ireland team at Ireland’s Lahinch Golf Club, Golf Channel’s Brentley Romine reported that multiple Americans were fighting “stomach issues.” Ethan Feng and William Jennings, Romine said, did not practice on Thursday, and three players didn’t attend that night’s banquet.

At a Friday press conference, though, Smith said every player would be ready for Saturday, though the Americans’ first alternate, Max Herendeen, has been contacted and is on “standby” — though he’s not on site.

Golf.title: A muni made me wait 30 mins on an empty course. Was that fair?
Golf.summary: In its quest to enforce the rules, the pro shop at a California muni lost sight of the bigger picture and alienated a customer. The post A muni made me wait 30 mins on an empty course. Was that fair? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I recently made a tee time at my local muni for the first twilight spot of the afternoon. I arrived at the course about 35 minutes early, paid my green fee and was on the putting green when I noticed that the 1st hole was wide open. I spoke to the starter, who told me I could go. But as I stepped up to the tee, the woman who’d checked me in burst from the pro shop and yelled at me to stop. Because I’d paid the discounted twilight rate, she said, I’d have to wait until twilight officially began. Never mind that there were no groups waiting to tee off. I looked plaintively at the starter, who shrugged. He was outranked. I tried to reason with the pro shop staffer, but she insisted that I couldn’t start my round. And so I waited for another 30 minutes, with the course empty in front of me and no other golfers teeing off.

To say that I was irritated is an understatement. I’m a regular at the course and the staffer’s decision struck me as spiteful and small-minded. Was I wrong to be annoyed? As we all know, rules are rules, and they’re meant to be followed. But sometimes they can also be harmlessly broken. Let’s say you’re playing a friendly match with a pal at a poorly conditioned course, and his ball lands in a footprint in the bunker. When he asks if he can move his ball without penalty, you say sure. Have you violated the letter of the law? Technically, yes. Have you made a reasonable decision? Also, yes. On the course, as off it, common sense and context should be our guides.

Golf.title: As the golf season winds down, Arccos keeps me improving
Golf.summary: I discovered a new area of golf focus on my Arccos app this month, and it's helping me understand my game beyond the clubs or the swing. The post As the golf season winds down, Arccos keeps me improving appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ve spent another month with Arccos game-tracking but this time most of my rounds were spent testing out upcoming club releases. It’s interesting to see what happens to my game when I’m not using my normal set, not to mention the new feature (or possibly one that I missed previously) that I’d love to dive into.

I’m still using the Arccos Air and the Arccos Smart Laser every time I play (as long as the course is rated) and both devices have been nothing but flawless. Now that I’ve been using the system for a good bit of time, the accuracy continues to improve and I am essentially at a point where I don’t even touch my phone or the app during my round, and everything is logged, no problem. Let’s use my August golf recap to see 1) where we’re at, 2) what clubs could land in the bag, and 3) what I still need to work on.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf star disqualified from DP World Tour Q School Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
As uncertainty around the future of LIV Golf continues to swirl, many of the league’s players are doing all they can to secure playing rights for the 2027 season. While the likes of Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton will have little concern about picking up starts on the DP World Tour, others are having to work a bit harder. That includes their Legion XIII teammate Caleb Surratt, who has entered a couple of HotelPlanner Tour events in recent weeks, and the trio of Luis Masaveu, Josele Ballester and Peter Uihlein, who all teed up in this week’s first stage of the DP World Tour’s grueling Q School experience.

With two rounds completed at Huddersfield Golf Club in England, Fireballs pair Masaveu and Ballester are still in the running at 2-under and 1-over respectively, but Uihlein has been disqualified after failing to show up for Friday’s third round – which is yet to get underway as strong winds wreak havoc in West Yorkshire.

Golf.body:
I’ve been trying to hold down the fort on being a blade putter user for a long time now, and I’m still holding out hope, but a few months ago during my first-ever putting lesson with Stephen Sweeney, I was convinced to give the mallet a real “college try.” Turns out, it’s been a game changer. Let’s dive into some of the facts and I’ll explain why the mallet is in my bag, but the trusty blade still sneaks in.

Within the first three minutes of the video, you’ll hear me state “yeah, well, blades are better” as Sweeney introduces our topic of the day, but writing this now four months later, a custom TaylorMade Spider Tour X has been in my bag ever since.

Golf.title: John Ashworth shares the keys to effortless on-course style
Golf.summary: When it comes to guidance for de-stressed on-course dressing, there’s only one guy for the job. Here are John Ashworth’s simple keys. The post John Ashworth shares the keys to effortless on-course style appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
For nearly five decades, there has been one universally agreed upon poster boy for effortless golf: Fred Couples. Beginning in the late ’80s, Couples’ on-course cool was buoyed by his apparel partnership with Ashworth, the laidback, SoCal brand founded by its namesake designer, John Ashworth. Player and polo were a perfect match.

Ashworth left the brand in 1997, only to return in 2024. Needless to say, when it comes to guidance for de-stressed on-course dressing, there’s only one guy for the job. Here are Ashworth’s keys for feeling effortless, because even the king of apparel cool would say that’s way more crucial than looking the part.

Golf.body:
After months of relative quiet, the attention of President Trump’s various building projects in Washington D.C. has turned to one of the district’s municipal courses, albeit with little certainty about the administration’s official plans.

This is the increasingly popular case of East Potomac Golf Links, a 36-hole muni property in the heart of D.C. that Trump has sought to renovate into an 18-hole championship golf course. In late June, President Trump targeted Sept. 1 as the official start date for construction on the course, and while heavy machinery arrived on-site this week, that date has now passed without much proof of significant course alterations.

Golf.body:
Ivy Shepherd’s putt fell on the 14th hole on Thursday at the U.S. Women’s Mid-Amateur and the tears fell soon after. It’d been a long, turbulent journey for Shepherd — one that had brought her to the heights of the collegiate amateur circuit and the doldrums of competitive golf. Now, for a few fleeting moments, it was complete.

She was a U.S. Women’s Mid-Am champion, and she was headed to the U.S. Women’s Open. “It’s awesome. It’s the longest freaking Women’s Open qualifier in the history of the world. But it’s cool,” Shepherd said. “All that is just awesome, you know, results and rewards for a long week of competitive golf for somebody who is going to end up winning it. Again, just tons of gratitude. Yeah, I feel very, very blessed.”

Five years ago, hybrids were still a regular part of bags on the PGA Tour. Even Rory McIlroy was using one. Today, they’re almost nonexistent, with only three PGA Tour winners across 37 events carrying one for their victory this past FedEx Cup season.

Meanwhile, the first two offerings in the new Mizuno Pro Signature Series, the S-1 and S-3, were a compact blade and a compact shallow cavity. Irons designed for elite ball strikers, but not as much for a player who wanted just a touch of forgiveness.

Golf.title: Jon Rahm’s LIV Golf Future Faces Uncertain Cliff
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm’s LIV Golf Future Faces Uncertain Cliff Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm stands at a crossroads that could define the rest of his career. The two-time major champion's future with LIV Golf looks shaky as the league tries to secure new funding. Reports suggest the breakaway tour might not keep him. This isn't just a small contract dispute. It involves a massive $150 million sum still owed to the Spanish star. As the league restructures, the man many called their flagship player might be walking away. The situation creates a ripple effect across professional golf, leaving fans wondering where the 31-year-old will play next season.

When Rahm jumped to the rebel tour in late 2023, he signed a deal loaded with cash. Per multiple reports, he is still owed around $150 million from that multi-year contract. That figure makes his position unique and complicated. As LIV Golf fights to bring in a new lead investor, reportedly BC Partners, the league's financial math changes. His contract now looks out of bounds for the new owners. Losing such a high-profile talent would be a huge blow to the league's credibility. LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil admitted the stakes were high. To reach and complete this transaction is the sole focus of our efforts. Without the players, that becomes very difficult, O'Neil said, as reported by reports. The pressure is on to close the deal while keeping stars like Rahm happy.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf staff 'struggling to pay mortgages and bills' as bankruptcy impact laid bare AOL.com
Golf.body:
Freelance workers say they have not been paid by LIV Golf as the troubled league prepares to declare bankruptcy. LIV is widely expected to file for voluntary bankruptcy in the coming days after the termination of Saudi Arabia's financial support. The Public Investment Fund (PIF), which launched LIV in 2022 and backed it with billions of dollars, announced in April that it was withdrawing its support, and the split was completed on Sep. 1.

The league has agreed terms in principle for a rescue package worth in the region of $300 million with private equity firm BC Partners. The deal has yet to be finalized, but LIV is confident of getting it over the line. Imminent bankruptcy, though, remains likely.

American golf brand Good Good has sacked two senior executives following backlash over an advert which showed a woman being pushed to the ground after reaching for a club. The company, whose YouTube channel has 2.1m subscribers, said it had parted ways with chief executive Matt Kendrick and president Joe Flannery following the release last month of the advert created for golf club manufacturer Callaway.

Good Good vice-president of brand and marketing Jeffrey Lefkovits was sacked earlier this week. Head of finance and operations at Good Good, Alex Puchala, said the dismissals on Wednesday were a "difficult day for the entire Good Good family".

Golf.title: How a Ryder Cup rules controversy kept Jason Day from the Presidents Cup

Golf.body:
When Presidents Cup rosters were finalized Tuesday, a few notable exclusions stood out. On the American side, captain Brandt Snedeker went with budding young star Jackson Koivun and Genesis Invitational winner Jacob Bridgeman over Ryder Cuppers Ben Griffin and J.J. Spaun. For the Internationals, one big name did not make Geoff Ogilvy’s squad: Jason Day.

The 2015 PGA Champion and former World No. 1 has played in five Presidents Cups and is one of the biggest names on an International side that lacks star power outside of Hideki Matsuyama and Adam Scott. But the 38-year-old Day dealt with a back injury for a big part of the 2026 season. It forced him to withdraw pre-tournament from the 3M Open and the Rocket Classic and contributed to Day missing the FedEx Cup Playoffs for the first time in 18 years.

Golf.title: Tiger Woods strikes plea deal in DUI case, has license suspended
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods reached a plea deal in a DUI case stemming from a March car accident and had his license suspended for five years. The post Tiger Woods strikes plea deal in DUI case, has license suspended appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Tiger Woods will be off the road for five years. On Wednesday morning, the 15-time major champion changed his plea in a DUI case stemming from his car accident in March and had his license suspended for five years as part of a deal to avoid jail time.

Woods was arrested in Jupiter, Fla. at the end of March on suspicion of driving under the influence after his car struck the back of a maintenance vehicle and flipped over on a one-lane road. Nobody was injured in the crash, but a short police investigation resulted in Woods failing a field sobriety test. Officers at the scene of the crash arrested Woods and charged him with DUI, and also recovered two pills inside his pocket that Woods identified as hydrocodone, a prescription opioid.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Hopes Screwing Its Own Players In Bankruptcy Will Secure Its Future
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Hopes Screwing Its Own Players In Bankruptcy Will Secure Its Future Defector
Golf.body:
LIV Golf recently sent out a mass email to mark the conclusion of its 2026 season. I imagine this was a somewhat slapdash operation given that the outfit, recently dumped by the Saudi Public Investment Fund, had to lop off the final event on its schedule, the team championship, which was scheduled for the final weekend of August, in Plymouth, Mich. Instead, the player championship and the team championship were both settled in Indianapolis, with stripped down entertainment offerings and drastically reduced player bonuses. In the week between the season's sudden conclusion and the arrival of the email, LIV Golf laid off a majority of its employees, writing in a statement to Golf Digest that the operation had "informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0" had concluded. Perhaps the exodus and confusion explain how they got the email wrong: Mine addressed me as "Dear LIV Golf Fan" and thanked me for supporting their terrible league. Not me! I've been to two LIV Golf events and both sucked mega shit.

The email encourages recipients to "stay tuned for more LIV Golf," without offering any details whatsoever about where a LIV Golf Fan might do that, or for how long. The promotion's future is very much up in the air. In the statement announcing the layoffs, a LIV Golf spokesperson insisted that whoever is left over there is still working "toward making LIV 2.0 a reality."

Golf.body:
Jon Rahm is set for a busy run on the golf course as he awaits news on LIV Golf's future, with the troubled league facing bankruptcy. Two-time major champion Rahm is believed to be the league's biggest creditor, still owed a nine-figure sum from the blockbuster contract he signed to jump ship from the PGA Tour in 2023.

The former world No. 1 has been linked with a return to the PGA Tour as LIV's future hangs in the balance, with some staff fearing that Rahm will quit regardless of whether a rescue deal funded by private equity firm BC Partners is finalized.

He pleaded not guilty the same month to misdemeanor charges of driving under the influence and refusal to submit to testing. Woods, 50, said he was seeking treatment after the incident.

To-date, the League has impacted more than one million young people’s lives through its Impact and Sustainability initiatives. Through its Game pillar, LIV Golf is actively removing historic barriers to entry and expanding access to the sport worldwide, exceeding its ambitious annual target to introduce 15,000 new youth to golf in 2026. This commitment to youth development is reflected globally through tailored regional programs and team initiatives.

The name is a nod to Lee’s on-course nickname, the Chef, which evolved from Lee’s “Let him cook” captions on social media.

Now, the PGA Tour winner and top-30 player is sporting his very own shoe. “I wanted a shoe that felt locked in and responsive when I’m swinging at full speed, but I also wanted it to look clean, premium and different from anything else out there,” Lee said in a release. “This was a true collaborative process with the PAYNTR Golf team, and we kept testing and refining the shoe until every detail felt right. The CHEF RX RS gives me the stability, comfort and traction I need to go after it while still representing my personality and style. I’m excited for golfers to experience our creation on the golf course.”

Golf.title: This driver shaft (and brand) continues to dominate the PGA Tour
Golf.summary: Fujikura didn't sweep the majors in 2026, but its Ventus lineup of shafts had more wins than any other brand. The post This driver shaft (and brand) continues to dominate the PGA Tour appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
A year after a Fujikura driver shaft swept all four major championships, they’re again at the top of the pecking order for winners on the PGA Tour. While Fujikura didn’t get the major sweep again in 2026, the company led the winning counts for driver shafts on the PGA Tour once again. Its Ventus line of shafts had more victories than any other brand’s entire catalog and the Ventus Black profile itself had as many victories as the second-place brand.

What’s also impressive is that the driver shaft market on the PGA Tour is effectively dominated by three brands, with Mitsubishi and Project X also having solid years this season.

Golf.title: LIV Golf on the verge of bankruptcy
Golf.summary: LIV Golf on the verge of bankruptcy Mundo Deportivo
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is facing a critical period. The men’s golf circuit, launched in 2022 by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, or PIF, has reportedly sought bankruptcy protection after laying off most of its workforce while continuing its search for a lead investor following the PIF’s withdrawal, according to the Financial Times.

The circuit recently sent settlement offers to current players who are owed millions of dollars in guaranteed payments extending beyond 2026. A bankruptcy filing could be submitted in federal district court in New Jersey, while the PIF is expected to provide less than $100 million in bankruptcy financing, without committing additional funds.

Bryson DeChambeau will once again be missing from Team USA’s Presidents Cup line-up due to his affiliation with LIV Golf. Brandt Snedeker will name his captain’s pick for the upcoming 2026 event at Medinah Country Club tonight.

Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Russell Henley and Collin Morikawa have qualified for the team outright and they will be joined by six more names. Chris Gotterup, Xander Schauffele, JJ Spaun and Justin Thomas will no doubt make the cut but Snedeker will have been thinking long and hard about the final two spots on his roster.

Golf.title: Tour Edge launches new Exotics Milled wedges with 17 loft/grind combinations
Golf.summary: Tour Edge is launching its new Exotics Milled Wedge Series featuring three different bounce profiles to match your swing. The post Tour Edge launches new Exotics Milled wedges with 17 loft/grind combinations appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Tour Edge continues to revamp its product line, and its latest introduction targets the short game. The company is announcing its new Exotics Milled Wedge Series featuring 17 different loft and grind combinations and a tri-sole design to give players options within the brand.

“Throughout my career, we’ve designed and produced wedges that both Tour players and amateurs love and trust,” CEO and lead designer Dave Glod said in a release. “This lineup takes that commitment to a new level, and I can’t wait for more golfers to discover Tour Edge as a true wedge destination.”

Golf.title: Rules Guy: If the group ahead is slow, can I take more than 3 minutes to find my ball?
Golf.summary: If you're waiting on the group ahead, can you use the extra time to search for your ball for more than 3 minutes? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: If the group ahead is slow, can I take more than 3 minutes to find my ball? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Let’s say, while playing behind a slow group, I hit my ball into an area where I can’t find it in the allotted 3 minutes. If I couldn’t play my next shot anyway because they’re delaying my pace of play, can I continue to look for my ball without penalty? – Barry Nygard, via email

It’s a reasonable thought, Barry…but reasonableness isn’t the standard here. The three-minute search time is a hard deadline, regardless of whether slowpokes would have had you waiting. Once you or your caddie (or your partner or partner’s caddie in partner formats) start to search for your ball, if it’s not found within that allotted three minutes it is lost and no longer in play, and Rule 18.2b requires that you play under stroke and distance. (See also Definition of Lost.)

Golf.title: The Future Is Bright For LIV Golf’s Youngest Winner
Golf.summary: The Future Is Bright For LIV Golf’s Youngest Winner livgolf.com
Golf.body:
The swagger was there from the start. The gold chain around his neck, visible and prominent thanks to his always-unbuttoned polo. The high-crowned cap that seemed a half-size larger than everybody else’s. The cocky demeanor balanced by the megawatt smile and funny charm of a 22-year-old determined to enjoy the moment at hand.

And, of course, those huge quadriceps, apparent even when wearing long pants and certainly intimidating whenever he wore shorts, the thin fabric unable to contain the ripples on display with every tee shot. At first glance, he looked less like a golfer and more like one of those rugby props doing battle on the front line of a scrum.

Golf.title: The winningest driver of the 2026 FedEx Cup season might surprise you
Golf.summary: For the second year in a row, the winningest driver of the FedEx Cup season was a 2024 model. See the full list of winningest drivers. The post The winningest driver of the 2026 FedEx Cup season might surprise you appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Make no mistake, 2026 was a driver year. That’s reflected in the bags of this year’s PGA Tour winners. Callaway, Ping, Srixon, TaylorMade and Titleist all had drivers released this year win on the PGA Tour this season, with TaylorMade and Titleist’s 2026 models winning multiple times.

But in the end, for the third straight season, it was actually a driver released in 2024 that took the cake as the winningest driver of 2026. With a whopping eight victories, three of them by Matt Fitzpatrick, Titleist’s GT3 was the winningest driver of 2026.

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's Tour Championship near-miss leads him to great 'philosophical question'
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland had the Tour Championship in his grasp before Scottie Scheffler grabbed it. That near-miss has Hovland facing a big question. The post Viktor Hovland’s Tour Championship near-miss leads him to great ‘philosophical question’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Viktor Hovland is both a big-picture thinker and someone who is myopically focused. Such is the blessing and curse of the gifted, those given rare talent and a brain that never stops tinkering.

So after watching Scottie Scheffler run past him on Sunday at the Tour Championship, Hovland looked at the 10,000-foot view of his season, one that saw him beat Scheffler in a playoff at the Travelers and hold the 54-hole lead at East Lake. It was a season in which he contended while still searching for the feeling that has been missing since he started re-working his swing after his 2023 FedEx Cup win. Viktor Hovland is still searching for Viktor Hovland. So, in that sense, it’s positive that he can still contend with and beat the best in the world while trying to reach through smoke to grab whom he used to be. But the other part of Hovland, the one who is focused on the small details of everything, saw himself lose the first 54-hole lead of his career because he’s still not that Viktor Hovland.

Badminton.title: Farewell to Titus Kurniadi
Badminton.summary: Farewell to Titus Kurniadi BWF Corporate
Badminton.body:
BWF mourns the passing of long-time administrator Titus Kurniadi on 31 August 2026 at the age of 89. Titus Kurniadi with 1992 women’s singles Olympic champion Susi Susanti. Kurniadi served the BWF (then IBF) Council from 1986 to 1994, almost all the time as an influential Chair of Finance and Member of the Chairman’s Board. Kurnaidi also contributed immensely to Indonesian badminton as Treasurer and Foreign Affairs representative for many years.

He served at a period when the IBF received its first substantial income from the Olympic Games in Barcelona and could begin to invest substantially in the future. Kurniadi’s words helped to convince a hesitant Council to introduce the World Team Championships for the Sudirman Cup by offering on behalf of PBSI the trophy. He oversaw the creation of this treasure that incorporates elements of Indonesian history, legend, and badminton heritage.

Badminton.title: How many BWF World Tour titles have Satwik-Chirag won after China Masters 2026?
Badminton.summary: How many BWF World Tour titles have Satwik-Chirag won after China Masters 2026? Sportstar
Badminton.body:
Indian men’s doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty added yet another BWF title to their kitty after winning the China Masters Super 750 tournament in Shenzhen, China on Sunday.

The World No.5 pair defeated China’s He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 to win their tenth World Tour doubles title together. The duo had also won the Singapore Open Super 750 event in May this year, their first title since 2024.

Badminton.title: China Masters: Super 750 Glory at First Asking
Badminton.summary: China Masters: Super 750 Glory at First Asking BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Sumire Nakade and Miyu Takahashi needed just one shot at the HSBC BWF World Tour Super 750 level to make history. The Japanese women’s pair continued their remarkable debut season at LI-NING China Masters 2026, beating fellow Super 750 debutants Bao Li Jing/Cao Zi Han 21-18 21-18 to claim their first title at this level.

“It feels unbelievable,” the 22-year-old Nakade said after the breakthrough triumph, while Takahashi, 24, admitted she was “very happy” despite a “tense final”. The victory adds another chapter to a sublime run for the pair, who have lost just twice since winning their first HSBC BWF World Tour event at the Orleans Masters in March. They have since lifted the US and Taipei Open titles, making it four victories from six World Tour tournaments.

Badminton.title: China Masters: Miyazaki Refuses to Blink, Defies Wang
Badminton.summary: China Masters: Miyazaki Refuses to Blink, Defies Wang BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Tomoka Miyazaki turned reflection into resilience on Saturday, producing a stunning comeback to defeat second-seeded local favourite Wang Zhi Yi 21-19 23-21 and reach the LI-NING China Masters 2026 final.

Badminton.body:
[OSEN=Ko Sung-hwan Reporter] Shim Yu-jin (27 years old, Incheon International Airport) failed to overcome the wall of Yamaguchi Akane (29), the "pride of Japanese badminton." World No. 16 Shim lost 0-2 (15-21, 16-21) to Yamaguchi (world No. 3) in the women’s singles Round of 16 match at the 2026 BWF World Badminton Federation (BWF) China Masters held at Shenzhen Arena in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, on September 3 (Korean time).

Shim, who advanced by easily defeating Song Shu-yun (Taiwan) 2-0 (21-9, 21-13) in the first round, challenged for her first win against Yamaguchi. She had lost all four previous meetings. Shim struggled to secure even a single game against the global powerhouse, leaving her with lingering regret.

Badminton.title: China Masters: Liu/Hsu Tame World Champs

Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue found their first test as world champions a painful one as Liu Kuang Heng/Hsu Yin-hui stunned them 23-21 21-10 in just 38 minutes in the LI-NING China Masters 2026 opening round on Wednesday.

Liu/Hsu produced a composed and aggressive display to subdue the French duo, who claimed the world title just two Sundays ago. Trailing 19-17, Liu/Hsu fought back to level the score before saving a game point and eventually closing out the game 23-21. That breakthrough proved decisive – with the pressure shifting firmly onto the French, Liu/Hsu raced through the second game 21-10.

Badminton.summary: Lakshya Sen vs Victor Lai live streaming: When and where to watch China Masters 2026 Sportstar
Badminton.body:
Lakshya Sen will begin his China Masters 2026 campaign against Canada’s Victor Lai on Wednesday, in a men’s singles opener shaped by a late change at the top of the draw. The Indian was originally due to meet newly crowned world champion Alex Lanier of France, but the Frenchman withdrew from the Super 750 event after his title-winning run at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi, handing Lakshya a more familiar test in Lai instead.

The pairing is anything but unknown territory. Lakshya and Lai have already met three times in 2026, including a gruelling contest at the All England Championships that stretched deep into a third game and underlined how evenly matched the two are. Lai arrives with the better recent form, having reached the semifinals at the Worlds, while Lakshya will be looking to respond after a second-round exit in New Delhi to the USA’s Garret Tan.

In the women's singles, Chen Yufei (world ranking 4th) and Han Yue (world ranking 5th) of China declared their absence. Additionally, the Chinese women's doubles pair Liu Shengshi-Tan Ning also withdrew.

Badminton.title: From watching Shin-chan, Doraemon and K-dramas to translating shuttlers' words for the world: How young interpreters found their way to badminton's biggest stage
Badminton.summary: From watching Shin-chan, Doraemon and K-dramas to translating shuttlers' words for the world: How young interpreters found their way to badminton's biggest stage timesofindia.indiatimes.com
Badminton.body:
, players weighed every word as carefully as their drop shots. But beyond the glare of the cameras, another contest was quietly unfolding. Standing a step behind the athletes were the interpreters, almost invisible yet carrying the immense responsibility of ensuring that nuance survived the journey from Mandarin, Japanese or Korean into English.

At a World Championships, where every word can travel as quickly as a smash, a mistranslated phrase can soften conviction, distort the meaning of an entire exchange or, in the worst case, trigger an unintended geopolitical controversy. For the interpreters, getting the words right is only part of the job. The real challenge is ensuring that nothing gets lost in translation.

Competitor News.title: EverPass Media Expands Netflix Partnership to Bring NFL Broadcasts to Venues Nationwide
Competitor News.summary: EverPass Media Expands Netflix Partnership to Bring NFL Broadcasts to Venues Nationwide Ministry of Sport
Competitor News.body:
EverPass Media has secured an expanded multi-year distribution agreement with Netflix to deliver the streaming giant’s complete National Football League content slate to commercial establishments across the United States.

Building on a successful prior collaboration that brought Christmas Day fixtures and live boxing events to hospitality venues, the partnership encompasses high-profile global fixtures, including the upcoming Week 1 Melbourne clash between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams, the league’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the 2027 NFL Honors ceremony.
